title: AiSOC Playbook
description: The authoring contract for AiSOC playbooks. Every step type listed in `properties.steps.items.properties.type.enum` is accepted by the runtime model (`services/agents/app/playbook/models.py::StepType`), and `x-aisoc-execution` records what the engine actually does with it. Kept in lockstep with the engine by `scripts/check_playbook_schema_parity.py`.

x-aisoc-execution.description: What `services/agents/app/playbook/engine.py` does with each step type. `executed` = a handler runs and has a real effect (an outbound call to a service, or engine-internal control flow). `governed` = the step is dispatched through the action registry in `services/actions`, where the capability contract and the tenant autonomy policy decide whether a vendor is touched; the step reports which happened and `executed` is the single field that means one was, so a preview, an approval queue and a missing integration are each named rather than reported as a success. `unimplemented` = no handler is registered; the engine fails the step closed rather than reporting a success it did not achieve. This map is machine-checked against the engine's handler table, so it cannot drift into an aspirational claim.

on.description: Event type that fires this playbook.

tags.description: Alert/case must carry at least one of these tags.

inputs.description: Authored documentation of the trigger-context fields this playbook expects. The engine does NOT bind, inject or validate these — a step reads its own values from `params` and from the run context. Present so a pack can describe its interface to a reader; do not treat it as a parameter-binding mechanism.

field.description: Dot-path on the trigger event where this input is expected to be found.

dry_run_support.description: Authored assertion that this playbook is safe to run with the engine's `dry_run` flag. The engine's `dry_run` applies uniformly to every step regardless of this value, so it is catalogue metadata rather than a runtime switch.

StepCondition.description: Structured condition form. Every field has a runtime default, so none is required; an empty object is a condition that always passes.

expression.description: Expression form, e.g. "inputs.source_ip != null". Mutually exclusive with field/operator/value; evaluated at runtime by the engine.

id.description: Short unique identifier within the playbook (used for branching).

type.description: The step verb. See `x-aisoc-execution` at the root of this schema for what the engine does with each one — a type listed there as `unimplemented` is a valid authoring vocabulary word that the engine will fail closed on rather than execute.

params.description: Step-specific parameters. Keys depend on the step type.

condition.description: Guard that must pass before the step runs. Accepts either an expression string or the structured form; the engine coerces a bare string into `{"expression": ...}`.

timeout_seconds.description: Per-step timeout. Ceiling mirrors `bounds.ABSOLUTE_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; long values exist for `approval` steps that wait on a human. Note that handlers reading `params.timeout_seconds` are separately clamped to `bounds.ABSOLUTE_MAX_PARAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

next_true.description: Step ID to jump to when condition is true (branching).

next_false.description: Step ID to jump to when condition is false (branching).
